questions.title: Higher mission and purpose
questions.question: What mission, purpose and responsible command does the higher order state for RESOLUTE HERALD?
questions.expected_answer: When directed, USEUCOM conducts integrated operations in the information environment, including MISO, cyberspace, electromagnetic-spectrum, public affairs and civil-military activities. The purpose is to preserve Moldova’s sovereign democratic process against coercion while deterring escalation and keeping US action below armed conflict.

criteria.text: Identifies USEUCOM as the responsible command.
Preserves the when-directed execution condition.
Identifies integrated operations in the information environment as the mission activity.
Identifies MISO as a stated capability group.
Identifies cyberspace activities as a stated capability group.
Identifies electromagnetic-spectrum activities as a stated capability group.
Identifies public affairs as a stated capability group.
Identifies civil-military activities as a stated capability group.
States protection of Moldova’s sovereign democratic process against coercion.
Preserves the below-armed-conflict ceiling.
Preserves the aim of deterring escalation.

acceptable_alternatives: Equivalent mission wording with the same purpose and limits.
error_conditions: Changes the mission to autonomous combat or treaty defence of Moldova.
questions.derivation_note: OIE is already explicitly identified as the main effort in the packet. The accepted essential-task item is therefore represented as source identification, with its accepted case preserved in the provenance.

questions.title: Partner-led end state and objectives
questions.question: Which partner-led end-state conditions and campaign objectives are stated?
questions.expected_answer: Moldovan and European institutions should visibly and credibly lead the information defence, while the campaign’s reach and deniability are degraded and escalation remains deterred below armed conflict. These are conditions sought, rather than a list of US activities.

criteria.text: Identifies visible and credible Moldovan/European institutional leadership.
Identifies degradation of campaign reach as an end-state condition.
Identifies degradation of campaign deniability as an end-state condition.
Preserves deterrence of escalation as a desired condition.
Preserves the armed-conflict ceiling.
Describes desired conditions rather than activities alone.

acceptable_alternatives: Equivalent condition statements retaining partner leadership.
error_conditions: Equates more US products or visibility with achievement of the end state.
questions.derivation_note: Retrieves the stated scenario information, preserving its status and qualifications.

questions.title: National attribution decisions
questions.question: What responsibilities are assigned for public attribution and intelligence disclosure?
questions.expected_answer: The command develops and maintains recommendations, but national authorities decide public attribution and intelligence release. USEUCOM cannot convert its own analytic confidence or recommendation into national release authority.

criteria.text: Distinguishes command recommendations from national decisions.
Identifies public attribution as a nationally retained decision.
Identifies intelligence disclosure as a nationally retained decision.

acceptable_alternatives: A concise recommendation-versus-decision distinction is sufficient.
error_conditions: Assigns final public attribution or intelligence-release authority to the command.
questions.derivation_note: Retrieves the stated scenario information, preserving its status and qualifications.

questions.title: Cyberspace coordination and restrictions
questions.question: What cyberspace coordination task and execution restrictions does the higher order state?
questions.expected_answer: Integrate cyberspace with USCYBERCOM. Stage offensive options without executing them. The baseline is defensive at Moldovan invitation, while offensive effects require national approval.

criteria.text: Identifies USCYBERCOM integration.
Distinguishes staging from executing offensive options.
Preserves invited defensive baseline.
Identifies national approval for offensive effects.

acceptable_alternatives: Equivalent authority-and-scope table.
error_conditions: Treats preparation of an offensive option as permission to execute it.
questions.derivation_note: Retrieves the stated scenario information, preserving its status and qualifications.

questions.title: Planning deliverable and deadline
questions.question: What organisational and planning deliverables are directed by higher headquarters, and by when?
questions.expected_answer: Establish a joint task force, complete mission analysis and submit a concept of operations to the Joint Staff no later than 10 September 2027. The deliverable deadline is distinct from the authority needed to execute each activity.

criteria.text: States establishment of a JTF.
States completion of mission analysis as a deliverable.
States submission of the CONOPS as a deliverable.
Gives the Joint Staff deadline as 10 September 2027.

acceptable_alternatives: Equivalent date format.
error_conditions: Treats timely submission as automatic permission to deploy or execute all proposed activities.
questions.derivation_note: Retrieves the stated scenario information, preserving its status and qualifications.

questions.title: Support consent and territorial scope
questions.question: What conditions govern US support and visible presence in the baseline operation?
questions.expected_answer: Moldova is a non-NATO, neutral partner with no US mutual-defence obligation. Support requires Moldovan request/consent and Chief-of-Mission authority for in-country activity. The baseline places visible military presence in Romania, while Moldova is the supported operating area. Expanded visible activity is not presumed approved.

criteria.text: Identifies absence of a mutual-defence obligation.
States the Moldovan request/consent condition.
States Chief-of-Mission authority for in-country activity.
Distinguishes Moldova support from visible presence in Romania.
Preserves the absence of automatic authority for expanded visible activity.

acceptable_alternatives: May mention the separately governed protection/evacuation sequel without treating it as the baseline.
error_conditions: Assumes existing consent authorises any expanded activity.
questions.derivation_note: Retrieves the stated scenario information, preserving its status and qualifications.

questions.title: Visibility risk and partner sensitivity
questions.question: What risk and partner sensitivities are stated concerning visible US activity?
questions.expected_answer: US action perceived as election interference could damage the partner government and reinforce the militarisation narrative. The packet identifies sensitivity to visible uniformed personnel in Chișinău, US-branded messaging and foreign personnel in electoral institutions, and states that consent can narrow.

criteria.text: States the partner-damage and interference-perception risk.
Identifies sensitivity to visible US uniformed personnel in Chișinău.
Identifies sensitivity to US-branded messaging.
Identifies sensitivity to foreign personnel in electoral institutions.
Retains the possibility of narrowing consent.

acceptable_alternatives: Equivalent descriptions retaining the difference between actual activity and its public attribution.
error_conditions: Treats greater US visibility as unconditionally beneficial.
questions.derivation_note: Retrieves the stated scenario information, preserving its status and qualifications.

questions.title: Election and transition horizon
questions.question: What fixed event and conditional continuation horizon does the packet state?
questions.expected_answer: The parliamentary election is fixed for 5 December 2027 and the campaign continues through and beyond it. Guidance envisages a post-election contested-legitimacy window through approximately D+30 before transition to Moldovan/European institutions. The election date is a fact, while the later window is an approximate planning horizon.

criteria.text: Gives 5 December 2027 as a fixed election date.
States continuation beyond voting day.
Identifies the approximately D+30 contested-legitimacy window.
Distinguishes the fixed date from the conditional/approximate horizon.

acceptable_alternatives: May give an approximate early-January horizon without inventing an unconditional end date.
error_conditions: Lists the election date as an assumption or ends the operation automatically on that date.
questions.derivation_note: Retrieves the stated scenario information, preserving its status and qualifications.

questions.title: Force quantity and duration
questions.question: What differences does the packet state between apportioned and allocated information-support and hunt-forward forces?
questions.expected_answer: A three-company MISTF and 90-day hunt-forward team are apportioned. Two companies and 60 days of hunt-forward support are allocated. The third company and the duration extension remain pending requests. The packet states that allocated cyber coverage misses election day and the later window.

criteria.text: States three versus two MISTF companies.
States 90 versus 60 days of hunt-forward support.
Keeps the additional company as a pending request.
Keeps the duration extension as a pending request.
Reports the stated election-period coverage gap.

acceptable_alternatives: Equivalent tabulation with apportionment and allocation clearly separated.
error_conditions: Counts a request as an allocated asset.
Invents exact team start/end dates not stated in the packet.
questions.derivation_note: Retrieves the stated scenario information, preserving its status and qualifications.

questions.title: Threat courses and warning
questions.question: What most-likely and most-dangerous courses of action and warning priorities are stated?
questions.expected_answer: The most likely is sustained perception pressure. The most dangerous is election-day disruption or a results-perception attack, with LOW confidence. Warning priorities include deeper access to the results chain and pre-staged false-results material. These are warning indicators, not confirmation that the dangerous course will occur.

criteria.text: Identifies the sustained campaign as most likely.
Identifies the election/results disruption as most dangerous with LOW confidence.
Identifies deeper results-chain access as a warning indicator.
Identifies pre-staged false-results material as a warning indicator.
Does not treat capability indicators as a confirmed decision to act.

acceptable_alternatives: Equivalent source-listed results-chain indicators.
error_conditions: Changes LOW confidence into a forecast of certainty.
questions.derivation_note: Retrieves the stated scenario information, preserving its status and qualifications.

questions.title: Approval timing constraint
questions.question: What timing constraint does the packet identify for product and attribution approvals?
questions.expected_answer: Routine and sensitive activities follow different release paths, with sensitive products and attribution routed through USEUCOM to national decision. The election is the fixed planning date and approval latency is a binding constraint, but the packet does not provide processing times for every approval.

criteria.text: Identifies differing approval paths.
Links approval completion to the fixed election calendar.
Avoids inventing measured approval durations.

acceptable_alternatives: A qualitative statement of the stated latency constraint is sufficient.
error_conditions: Assigns a specific approval turnaround unsupported by the packet.
questions.derivation_note: Retrieves the stated scenario information, preserving its status and qualifications.

questions.title: Coordination and independent partners
questions.question: What standing coordination arrangements and partner roles are stated?
questions.expected_answer: The staff is directed to coordinate through a combined mechanism with EEAS/EUPM liaison. The JTF coordinates rather than commands external actors. OSCE/ODIHR provides neutral observation, and partners can differ in timing, visibility and attribution positions.

criteria.text: Identifies combined coordination with EEAS/EUPM.
Distinguishes coordination from command of external partners.
Identifies OSCE/ODIHR’s neutral observation role.
Retains potential divergence between partner positions.

acceptable_alternatives: Equivalent institutional names and coordination description.
error_conditions: Assumes the JTF can order an observer finding or dictate all partner timing.
questions.derivation_note: The coordination mechanism is explicitly directed in the supplied packet, so it remains A despite the original rubric’s implied-task phrasing.

questions.title: Narrative centre of gravity and requirements
questions.question: What centre of gravity, requirements and vulnerabilities does the JIPOE state for the campaign?
questions.expected_answer: It identifies coherence and perceived credibility of the narrative as the operational centre of gravity, with authenticity, deniability and synchronisation as requirements. Exposure of inauthenticity and loss of deniability are stated vulnerabilities. These are the supplied intelligence assessment.

criteria.text: Identifies coherence/perceived narrative credibility.
Identifies authenticity as a stated campaign requirement.
Identifies deniability as a stated campaign requirement.
Identifies synchronisation as a stated campaign requirement.
Relates inauthenticity exposure to the stated vulnerability.
Attributes the assessment to the supplied JIPOE.

acceptable_alternatives: Equivalent summary retaining requirements versus vulnerabilities.
error_conditions: Presents the supplied framing as an independently validated causal finding.
questions.derivation_note: Retrieves the stated scenario information, preserving its status and qualifications.

questions.title: Assessment observability limits
questions.question: What distinction does the packet make between observable activity and campaign effects?
questions.expected_answer: Products, reach and characterised networks are activity/performance measures. Audience behaviour and adversary decisions are harder to observe, with decision shifts assessed through proxies. The packet warns against treating campaign volume as campaign effect.

criteria.text: Distinguishes activity measures from effects.
States that decision-shift measures rely on proxies.
Preserves limits on direct observation of intent or effect.

acceptable_alternatives: Equivalent MOP/MOE terminology.
error_conditions: Treats product counts as direct proof of changed decisions.
questions.derivation_note: Retrieves the stated scenario information, preserving its status and qualifications.

questions.title: Strategic assumptions
questions.question: What assumptions concerning the ceasefire and Russian objectives are inherited from higher headquarters?
questions.expected_answer: The 18 March 2027 Russia–Ukraine ceasefire is assumed to hold, with Russian objectives remaining below armed conflict. The packet states that renewed war could divert capacity from Moldova and alter escalation calculations. These are planning assumptions and conditional assessments.

criteria.text: Identifies the ceasefire-holds assumption with its date.
Identifies the inherited below-threshold objective assumption.
States possible Russian capacity diversion if the ceasefire fails.
States that ceasefire failure can change escalation calculations.
Preserves assumption/conditional status.

acceptable_alternatives: Equivalent phrasing without asserting a probability or timing of failure.
error_conditions: Treats renewed war as a guaranteed end of pressure on Moldova.
questions.derivation_note: Retrieves the stated scenario information, preserving its status and qualifications.

questions.title: Energy dependency
questions.question: What electricity dependency and alternative supply limits does the packet state?
questions.expected_answer: Russian-owned Cuciurgan/MGRES supplies the majority, roughly 70–80%, of right-bank demand. Romanian interconnection exists but is capacity-limited and costlier. Winter heating demand increases the importance of the shortfall. No quantified remaining import margin is supplied.

criteria.text: Identifies Russian ownership of Cuciurgan/MGRES.
Identifies its majority contribution to right-bank electricity demand.
Identifies the limited Romanian interconnection alternative.
Relates winter demand to the supply problem.
Avoids inventing available replacement megawatts.

acceptable_alternatives: Majority rather than an exact percentage is acceptable if the dependency is clear.
error_conditions: Assumes the interconnector can replace all lost supply.
questions.derivation_note: Retrieves the stated scenario information, preserving its status and qualifications.

questions.title: Operational and end-state distinction
questions.question: How should progress against the campaign’s stated vulnerabilities be related to the partner-led end state?
questions.expected_answer: Degrading a campaign requirement can support the objective, but does not by itself establish credible partner leadership, preserved consent or below-threshold success. Operational progress and the wider end-state conditions therefore need separate checks.

criteria.text: Relates degraded campaign requirements to an intermediate operational objective.
Identifies credible partner leadership as an additional end-state condition.
Identifies the armed-conflict/escalation restraint as an additional end-state condition.
Rejects equivalence between intermediate progress and end-state achievement.

acceptable_alternatives: May use distinct objective and end-state indicators rather than those exact labels.
error_conditions: Declares mission success from exposure or output counts alone.
questions.derivation_note: Compares two specified constructs and identifies the conditions not entailed by one another.

questions.title: Authority-readiness assessment
questions.question: What does completion of planning and technical preparation establish about readiness to execute the proposed activities?
questions.expected_answer: It establishes neither national attribution release nor authority for offensive effects or expanded visible activity. Recommendations, preparation, invitation and each applicable approval are distinct prerequisites. A single undifferentiated ready status would conceal which activity remains conditional.

criteria.text: Separates completed planning/preparation from execution authority.
Distinguishes national approval from technical capability and partner invitation.
Identifies the need for activity-specific readiness status.

acceptable_alternatives: A conditional-readiness assessment by activity is acceptable.
error_conditions: Treats the EXORD title, submitted CONOPS or staged option as unrestricted execution authority.
questions.derivation_note: Combines distinct task and authority clauses to assess the validity of a consolidated readiness claim.

questions.title: Critical-period force coverage
questions.question: How should the allocated force and duration figures be assessed against the campaign horizon?
questions.expected_answer: The company shortage and time-coverage shortage are different constraints. The 60-day allocation is reported to miss the election period, and neither an apportioned 90-day figure nor a pending extension establishes actual dated coverage through all later requirements. Exact start/end dates and handover arrangements are needed to substantiate coverage.

criteria.text: Distinguishes force-quantity and duration shortages.
Preserves the stated allocated election-period gap.
Recognises that nominal duration alone does not establish dated coverage through the full horizon.
Avoids assuming a specific start date or automatic post-election coverage.

acceptable_alternatives: Can distinguish the D+3 results period from the broader approximate D+30 transition window.
error_conditions: Assumes the pending 90-day request proves full post-election coverage.
questions.derivation_note: Cross-checks force quantities and nominal durations against several distinct required periods; source labels alone are not treated as a dated coverage schedule.

questions.title: Consent and visibility assessment
questions.question: What does the stated consent posture imply for judging a change in the visible US footprint?
questions.expected_answer: Existing consent and a Romania-based baseline cannot be treated as approval for an increased visible footprint in Chișinău. The actual or publicly attributed footprint must be compared with the current invitation and Chief-of-Mission/national limits because visibility can undermine the partner purpose even without a change in technical capability.

criteria.text: Distinguishes baseline consent from expanded visible activity.
Relates actual or attributed presence to partner risk.
Preserves the applicable approval and coordination boundaries.

acceptable_alternatives: A task-by-task scope comparison is acceptable.
error_conditions: Infers unrestricted visible presence from a general assistance request.
questions.derivation_note: Combines consent scope, geographical baseline and reported sensitivity to identify the relevant changing variable.

questions.title: Deadline and approval assessment
questions.question: How should the CONOPS deadline and election calendar be related to activity approval readiness?
questions.expected_answer: A plan can be due before all execution approvals are obtained. Readiness for the intended support period depends on each approval’s scope and completion time, which the packet does not quantify. Compliance with the 10 September deliverable does not establish permission or timely availability for every proposed activity.

criteria.text: Separates the submission milestone from execution approval.
Relates approval completion to the activity’s required time.
Keeps unspecified processing durations unresolved.

acceptable_alternatives: A critical-path description with unresolved approval durations is acceptable.
error_conditions: Invents guaranteed approval dates or treats the submission deadline as release authority.
questions.derivation_note: Combines an administrative milestone with a later operational horizon and different approval paths.

questions.title: Independent observation assessment
questions.question: How does the OSCE’s role affect the staff’s use of observer findings in assessing mission progress?
questions.expected_answer: Independent observation can inform the legitimacy assessment, but its findings and publication timing are not controlled by the JTF. A staff plan that treats a favourable or timely observer finding as a commanded deliverable has an unsupported dependency.

criteria.text: Relates observer findings to the legitimacy assessment.
Preserves observer independence and lack of JTF control.
Identifies an unsupported dependency if favourable or timely findings are assumed.

acceptable_alternatives: Equivalent distinction between coordinating access and controlling conclusions.
error_conditions: Treats neutral observers as tasked producers of a predetermined favourable judgement.
questions.derivation_note: Derives the staff-planning implication of relying on an independent actor’s product.

questions.title: Assessability of proposed options
questions.question: What would reliance on product-release counts alone establish about the assessability of a proposed option’s claimed outcome?
questions.expected_answer: It would establish that output volume can be observed, but not that the claimed outcome can be assessed. The option still needs an obtainable outcome-linked indicator and a justified interpretation of any proxy. A readily countable activity cannot by itself substantiate an effectiveness ranking or prove a causal change in beliefs or decisions.

criteria.text: Distinguishes observable output volume from an outcome-linked indicator.
Identifies the missing outcome-measurement basis for an effectiveness comparison.
Preserves the uncertainty of proxy interpretation.
Rejects a causal-effect claim based only on product counts.

acceptable_alternatives: A qualitative assessability judgement supported by named observables is acceptable.
error_conditions: Rates the most prolific output producer as necessarily most effective.
questions.derivation_note: Applies the supplied output/effect distinction to a specific deficient option-assessment basis. It does not claim that the general distinction or use of proxies is newly inferred.

questions.title: Assumption-change assessment
questions.question: How would failure of the ceasefire assumption affect use of the current planning baseline?
questions.expected_answer: It would require rechecking both Russian capacity assigned to Moldova and the escalation context. Reduced available capacity would not automatically prove reduced risk, because the broader escalation situation could change in another direction. The current estimates should not simply be retained or uniformly scaled down.

criteria.text: Identifies the capacity estimate as dependent on the ceasefire assumption.
Identifies escalation calculations as dependent on the ceasefire assumption.
Rejects automatic reduction of overall risk from possible resource diversion.
Treats the change as conditional rather than an observed event.

acceptable_alternatives: Different directional assessments are acceptable if they retain uncertainty and justify both dependencies.
error_conditions: Concludes that ceasefire failure automatically ends the Moldova mission.
questions.derivation_note: Distinguishes the two consequences of assumption failure instead of treating resource diversion as a sufficient proxy for overall risk.

questions.title: Replacement-power adequacy
questions.question: What can be concluded about replacement electricity supply from the stated energy dependency and backstop?
questions.expected_answer: The existence of a Romanian interconnection does not establish adequate replacement for the lost Cuciurgan contribution during winter. A capacity-limited backstop and unknown import margin leave the residual service shortfall unresolved. No specific deficit can be calculated from the supplied information.

criteria.text: Distinguishes the existence of an alternative from adequate replacement capacity.
Relates the capacity limit to the high original dependency and winter demand.
Leaves the numerical shortfall unresolved.

acceptable_alternatives: A conditional partial-replacement assessment is acceptable.
error_conditions: Claims complete replacement or invents a megawatt deficit.
questions.derivation_note: Compares the magnitude and timing of demand with the bounded alternative without inventing missing capacity.

questions.title: End-of-support assessment
questions.question: What should distinguish readiness to transfer the support effort from reaching election day or a single defensive milestone?
questions.expected_answer: Neither election day nor one completed protection task establishes that partners can sustain all required functions. The results-publication period and the longer contested-legitimacy window have different needs, so transition needs function-specific continuity and partner acceptance, not a calendar-only decision.

criteria.text: Distinguishes the election, results period and broader transition horizon.
Separates a completed task from sustained partner capacity.
Identifies functional continuity as a transition consideration.
Identifies receiving-partner acceptance as a transition consideration.

acceptable_alternatives: A staged transfer assessment may allow different functions to transition at different times.
error_conditions: Treats D+3 or election day as an automatic end to every support function.
questions.derivation_note: Compares distinct phase requirements and the partner-led end state to assess whether a calendar milestone is sufficient.

questions.title: Escalation and partner-purpose criterion
questions.question: What criterion should be applied when comparing support options against the stated purpose?
questions.expected_answer: Include an explicit comparison of the potential to provide an escalation pretext or undermine partner leadership and consent, alongside the intended operational benefit. Document which approval is required for a material risk and reject treating technical feasibility alone as sufficient.

criteria.text: Defines escalation-pretext exposure as a comparison criterion.
Includes compatibility with partner leadership as a comparison condition.
Includes compatibility with current partner consent as a comparison condition.
Links a material approval-dependent risk to the appropriate decision before commitment.

acceptable_alternatives: Qualitative ordinal comparison is acceptable without unsupported numerical probabilities.
error_conditions: Recommends an option solely because it can be technically executed.
questions.derivation_note: Derives a concrete comparison and commitment condition from the non-equivalence of intermediate benefit and end-state success.

questions.title: Activity-specific permission gate
questions.question: What control should the staff establish before treating proposed activities as executable?
questions.expected_answer: For each proposed activity, record the responsible decision authority, current approval status, authorised scope and partner-consent condition, separately from technical readiness and planning completion. Hold the affected activity until the applicable permissions are confirmed, without assuming that another activity’s approval transfers.

criteria.text: Requires the responsible decision authority to be recorded for each activity.
Requires the current approval status to be recorded for each activity.
Requires the authorised scope to be recorded for each activity.
Requires the applicable partner-consent condition to be recorded for each activity.
Separates permission from technical and planning readiness.
Makes commitment conditional on confirmation of the applicable approvals.
Makes commitment conditional on confirmation of the applicable partner consent.

acceptable_alternatives: A release checklist or approval matrix is acceptable.
error_conditions: Uses one blanket ready flag to authorise all activity types.
questions.derivation_note: Adds an explicit readiness gate and separation of status dimensions to the source authority inventory.

questions.title: Dated force-coverage confirmation
questions.question: What force-management action should precede accepting coverage of the critical and transition periods?
questions.expected_answer: Obtain confirmed dates and scope for allocated cyber coverage, the extension decision and any authorised handover arrangement, and align them with the election/results and transition needs. Maintain a plan for confirmed resources while submitting or tracking the shortfall request. Treat company numbers and duration coverage as separate requirements.

criteria.text: Requests dated allocated availability.
Requests the duration-extension decision status.
Requests the status of any authorized handover arrangement.
Checks coverage against distinct critical and transition periods.
Keeps the baseline within confirmed resources while tracking unmet requirements.
Separates quantity shortfalls from duration shortfalls.

acceptable_alternatives: A dated coverage matrix with a contingency handover is acceptable; no particular extra unit is prescribed.
error_conditions: Claims a pending 90-day figure proves all calendar coverage.
questions.derivation_note: The source already recommends an extension. The new consequence requires verified calendar coverage and a resource-bounded handover rather than copying the RFF recommendation.

questions.title: Visible-footprint information requirement
questions.question: What friendly-force information requirement follows for controlling the visible support footprint?
questions.expected_answer: Track visible US uniformed presence in Chișinău and US military activity publicly attributed within Moldova, together with the applicable consent and approval status. Escalate changes outside the permitted baseline for review before expanding or continuing the affected activity. Do not invent a numerical personnel ceiling.

criteria.text: Requests the current visible US uniformed presence.
Requests the US military activity publicly attributed within Moldova.
Links the information to current consent/approval scope.
Defines review or adjustment of the affected activity as its decision use.

acceptable_alternatives: An FFIR with qualitative change triggers is acceptable.
error_conditions: Treats public attribution of presence as proof that the activity was authorised.
questions.derivation_note: Specifies a concrete observable and a footprint-control decision rather than only asking whether consent exists.

questions.title: Approval schedule information requirement
questions.question: What should the staff do if an activity approval cannot be confirmed by the intended support window?
questions.expected_answer: Keep the affected activity pending rather than treat CONOPS submission as execution clearance. Identify the support window and dependent commitments affected, and seek revised timing or an alternative within confirmed authority through the responsible decision offices. Update the shared schedule after that decision. Do not invent an approval turnaround time or assume that a fixed election deadline waives the approval.

criteria.text: Retains a pending status for the activity until its required approval is confirmed.
Identifies the support window or dependent commitments affected by the delay.
Seeks revised timing or an alternative within confirmed authority through the responsible decision offices.
Keeps plan submission distinct from execution clearance.

acceptable_alternatives: Deferral, resequencing or another independently authorized support activity is acceptable when its implications are made explicit.
A changed-support decision record may implement the same action as an updated schedule.
error_conditions: Executes the activity to meet the deadline despite missing required approval.
Assumes a requested alternative has inherited permission from the delayed activity.
questions.derivation_note: The source already orders an approval picture and timeline mapping (D10:38). The newly derived task is the conditional staff response to an approval that cannot meet the required window, including withholding the affected commitment and seeking an authorized schedule or support change.

questions.title: Independent-findings review provision
questions.question: What planning provision follows when progress assessment depends on independent observer findings?
questions.expected_answer: Establish liaison for lawful access to the findings and a review point that can use favourable, adverse or delayed reporting without presuming its content. Update the staff’s legitimacy assessment when findings arrive and preserve observer independence. Do not direct the result or treat its timing as a JTF-controlled milestone.

criteria.text: Requires an appropriate access or liaison arrangement for observer findings.
Requires a review provision for findings when available.
Allows adverse or delayed findings rather than a predetermined result.
Preserves observer independence in the resulting assessment.

acceptable_alternatives: A conditional assessment branch is acceptable.
error_conditions: Tasks observers to produce favourable findings or treats coordination as command.
questions.derivation_note: Converts an external analytical dependency into a concrete review and contingency provision.

questions.title: Assessability comparison requirement
questions.question: What action should follow when an option’s proposed outcome indicator is unavailable or cannot distinguish the intended outcome from activity volume?
questions.expected_answer: Task the assessment staff to verify an obtainable source and a usable outcome-linked indicator, or to develop and check a defensible alternative measurement plan. Arrange the necessary authorized data access or monitoring before crediting the claimed effect in the option comparison. If no adequate measure can be obtained, refer that specific assessability limitation to the decision authority and make any selection conditional on accepting it, rather than award an unsupported effectiveness advantage.

criteria.text: Requires verification or development of an obtainable outcome-linked indicator.
Requires the necessary authorized data access or monitoring arrangement.
Withholds an effectiveness advantage based only on unsupported outcome measurement.
Refers an unresolved assessability limitation for explicit decision acceptance.

acceptable_alternatives: A verified alternative indicator or a revised assessment design can satisfy the requirement.
The commander may accept a documented assessment limitation; this does not convert it into measured effectiveness.
error_conditions: Uses output volume as a substitute outcome without justification.
Treats a proxy as direct verification of internal decisions or causal impact.
questions.derivation_note: The sources already require separating outputs, outcomes and proxies. The new consequence is a measurement-feasibility task and a condition on how the option may be credited or selected when its proposed indicator is unavailable.

questions.title: Assumption-triggered plan revision
questions.question: What staff action should be specified if the ceasefire assumption fails?
questions.expected_answer: Trigger a review of the Moldova capacity estimate and escalation assumptions separately, identify affected support tasks and submit necessary changes through the existing command and national-approval arrangements. Preserve authorised tasks that remain justified while revising unsupported commitments. Do not equate resource diversion with an automatic reduction in all risks.

criteria.text: Triggers review of the Moldova capacity estimate.
Triggers review of the escalation estimate.
Identifies and revises affected support commitments.
Preserves the required command/national decision process.

acceptable_alternatives: A branch-planning task with explicit review products is acceptable.
error_conditions: Unilaterally expands military activity because the ceasefire has failed.
questions.derivation_note: Derives the concrete re-estimation and task-revision process from two potentially divergent effects of assumption failure.

questions.title: Power-backstop verification requirement
questions.question: What support-planning requirement follows before relying on the electricity backstop?
questions.expected_answer: Obtain a verified comparison of expected demand, remaining supply and available import capacity for the relevant winter period through the responsible partner/interagency channels. Identify the residual service gap and refer any additional support requirement for coordination before asserting that the backstop provides adequate resilience.

criteria.text: Requests expected electricity demand for the relevant period.
Requests remaining supply for the relevant period.
Requests available import capacity for the relevant period.
Uses the comparison to identify a residual service gap.
Coordinates additional support instead of asserting unsupported adequacy.

acceptable_alternatives: A power-support capacity check or decision-linked information requirement is acceptable; no specific engineering remedy is mandated.
error_conditions: Invents a replacement supply allocation or declares the full gap closed.
questions.derivation_note: Turns an unresolved adequacy judgement into a specific support-capacity verification requirement.

questions.title: Function-specific handover check
questions.question: What requirement should precede ending a support function during transition?
questions.expected_answer: Check the receiving institution’s agreed responsibility and ability to sustain that function across its remaining required period, with a continuity arrangement for outstanding gaps. Submit staged handover for the appropriate decision against those checks rather than a single election-day or D+3 cut-off for every function.

criteria.text: Requires confirmation of receiving institutional responsibility.
Requires confirmation that the receiving institution can sustain the function.
Matches the check to the function’s remaining required period.
Requires continuity arrangements for outstanding gaps.
Allows separately authorized staged handover by function.

acceptable_alternatives: A function-specific handover checklist with partner acceptance is acceptable.
error_conditions: Ends all support solely because election day has passed.
questions.derivation_note: Specifies a concrete handover check linking partner capacity and distinct time horizons. Handover is submitted to the responsible authority; the staff answer does not itself grant a new execution permission.

notes: The source strongly pre-specifies assessments and recommended tasks. New B/F nodes therefore test distinct comparisons, commitment prerequisites and verification/handover requirements, not rote repetition of those recommendations.
Nominal 60/90-day durations cannot by themselves prove calendar coverage without confirmed start/end dates. No unprovided service dates are inferred.
The campaign codename item is excluded because no substantive dependency uses the label. The Gagauzia-specific negative item is preserved but not attached outside its applicable scope.
All newly constructed questions, references and chains require military-expert validation. The accepted v0.4 inclusion decisions and case metadata remain preserved.

Independent construction review sharpened F005/F007 to distinguish existing source instructions from the newly derived conditional action, applied B007 to a deficient measurement basis, and kept F010 handover authority explicit.

Independent graph review moved the mission-scope parent in CH008 to the consequence step. Independent factual and decision conditions were split into separate scoring atoms; true comparison relations were retained.

Final criterion atomicity review split independent enumerated capabilities, approval conditions and requested facts without changing question wording, references or graph membership. Genuine relational comparisons remain intact.

Final dependency review replaced generic counterfactual wording with scenario-specific qualitative checks. These are unexecuted construction annotations for expert review, not empirical intervention results.
